targets.name: health
targets.rationale: Death (health 0) ends the episode; its one-step change prices every hazard the agent faces.

targets.name: food
targets.rationale: Hunger is the slowest vital clock; predicting its decrement and its refill (eating a cow or plant) tests a model of time and of eating.

targets.name: drink
targets.rationale: Thirst decrements faster than food and refills only beside water; predicting it tests whether the agent knows where water is.

targets.name: energy
targets.rationale: Fatigue is restored only by sleeping, which also exposes the agent to attack; its dynamics differ from the other vitals.

targets.name: wood
targets.rationale: Collect_wood is the first achievement on every tech path and wood is consumed by crafting; its change tests whether the agent knows what its own next action does.

targets.name: stone
targets.rationale: Stone requires a wood pickaxe to collect and is consumed by placing and crafting; it is the second rung of the tech tree.

utility.description: Count of distinct achievements unlocked in the episode (brief 1 section 3). Hafner's (2022) aggregate score is reported separately and is not the per-episode utility.

price.rationale: The exchange rate of compute into this World's per-episode utility (brief 1 A4 item 4), in achievements per CPU-second and per gigabyte-second (1e9 bytes) of peak memory, moved unchanged from judge/config.toml's [price.crafter] (brief 2 A2). Committed before the first scored run; never tuned after a score is seen. Derivation: an episode that exhausts every allowance of judge/config.toml's [candidate] and [timeouts] (cpus = 1.0 CPUs and memory_mib = 1024 MiB for episode_s = 600 s) is charged delta = 0.5 achievements, half for each resource. 0.5 is the smallest effect brief 1's FIT criterion requires the court to detect: priced lower, a candidate's whole allowance would cost less than any difference the court resolves, and compute would be free in every adoption decision; priced higher, compute would outweigh utility differences the court does resolve. So cpu_s = (delta / 2) / (cpus * episode_s) = 0.25 / 600 and memory_gb_s = (delta / 2) / (memory_mib * 2**20 / 1e9 * episode_s) = 0.25 / (1.073741824 * 600). The pricing rule is judge/price.py's: what the judge could not measure is charged at the configured limit.

rationale: Observation is the crafter package's semantic map (info['semantic']: the whole 64x64 world, material ids then object ids in SemanticView's order, index 0 unused) and inventory (info['inventory']), as brief 1 section 3 specifies; image observations are out of scope. Targets are six inventory counts one step ahead: the four vitals, whose dynamics are driven by the World, and the first two resources, whose dynamics are driven by the agent's own action. Six of sixteen keeps the set small while covering both kinds; the other ten inventory counts are zero for most of an untrained agent's steps and would score near-trivially.
